name: ObsessionBench
tagline: ObsessionDB vs ClickHouse Cloud on ClickBench: latency, consistency and cost, measured in the open.

scenarios.label: Data load
scenarios.description: Create the standard ClickBench `hits` table and load the same 10 million rows (the first 10 partitioned ClickBench parquet files) into each service. The load runs server-side from the public dataset URLs, so the sandbox never holds the data. Timed from first insert to the final row count matching.

scenarios.label: ClickBench, warm
scenarios.description: All 43 ClickBench queries, one client. Each query runs once untimed as a warm-up, then 5 timed runs. Per-query p50 and p99 come from the timed runs; suite time is the sum of per-query medians.

scenarios.label: Concurrent load
scenarios.description: 4 clients each run the 43 queries in a shuffled order (same seed for every contender) for 3 rounds after the warm-up. Reports p99 latency across all queries and how many failed, to show consistency under load. 4 clients keeps the smallest instance (8 GB) inside its memory; failures are still recorded, never hidden.
